title: Brad Pitt's Trick to Handle Awkward Topics
summary: This video breaks down Brad Pitt's strategy for addressing awkward or taboo public topics using a three-step method called Name, Defuse, and Pivot. The creator explains that acknowledging the elephant in the room immediately drops tension and helps people actually listen to you.
key_points: Name, defuse, and pivot strategy: First name what everyone is thinking, second defuse it by making yourself the joke, and third pivot to your main message.

Brad Pitt example: At the SAG awards during his tabloid divorce frenzy, Brad joked, 'I gotta add this to my Tinder profile... let's be honest, it was a difficult part. A guy who gets high, takes his shirt off, and doesn't get on with his wife.'
Why it works: The second you say the thing everyone is already thinking, they stop bracing for it and start actually listening to you.
Apply it to: A failed project, a resume gap, or something you shouldn't have said.
content: Brad Pitt trick to handle an awkward topic. Brad Pitt has a trick to handle the elephant in the room, and you can borrow it too, the next time there's something that everyone's thinking, but they're embarrassed to say it out loud. In 2020, he was in the tabloids all the time because of his high-profile breakup with his wife, Angelina Jolie. So, when he took the stage at the Screen Actors Guild Awards to accept the award for his role in Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, he knew what was on everyone's mind. I used to work as a presidential campaign spokesperson, so I spent a lot of time coaching people through how to handle difficult moments in public. And Brad handled it perfectly. Watch what he did. I got to add this to my Tinder profile. Let's be honest, it was a difficult part. A guy who gets high, takes his shirt off, and doesn't get on with his wife. Most people try to avoid the awkward subject altogether. They just hope it'll go away, but of course it doesn't. Everyone's just waiting for them to address it. But Brad does something different and it lets him capture and keep the audience's attention. He uses what I call the name, defuse, and pivot strategy. First, he names what everyone's thinking. He's describing the role, but everyone knows he's also talking about his own marriage. Second, he defuses it. He makes himself the joke so the tension drops and the room relaxes. The joke at the beginning about adding the award to his Tinder profile was perfect. And third, he pivots straight into a warm, gracious thank you to his co-stars. So, here's why this technique works. The second you say the thing that everyone's already thinking, they stop bracing for it and they start actually listening to you. So, the next time you've got an elephant in the room, maybe it's a project that failed or a gap in your resume or something you said that you shouldn't have, just name, defuse, and pivot so you can move on.
